h1: US Visa Appointment Wait Times in Nigeria: Among the Shortest in the World
deck: The assumption is that West African applicants wait longest. In August 2026 Abuja was booking visitor interviews inside about two weeks while Toronto sat past sixteen months, and almost nobody has noticed the inversion.

coverSpec.title: West African posts had some of the shortest US visitor visa queues in the world in August 2026
coverSpec.desc: In August 2026 the interview-required B-1/B-2 wait was about 15 days at Abuja, about 30 days at Lagos and about 105 days at Accra, against about 495 days at Toronto, about 435 at Sydney and about 315 at Hyderabad. The longest visitor visa queues in the world are now in wealthy English-speaking countries, not in West Africa, and for Nigerian applicants the binding constraint is documentation and administrative processing rather than the appointment calendar.

faq.q: How long is the US visa appointment wait in Nigeria?
faq.a: Short, by world standards. In August 2026 the interview-required B-1/B-2 wait was about 15 days at Abuja and about 30 days at Lagos. Student, petition-based and crew categories were around 15 days at both posts. For comparison, Toronto was near 495 days and Sydney near 435 in the same snapshot.

faq.q: Is Abuja or Lagos faster for a US visa interview?
faq.a: In August 2026 Abuja was the faster of the two for visitor visas, at about 15 days against about 30 at Lagos, and both were quick in absolute terms. At queues this short the difference is rarely worth travelling for, and which post you may use is decided by your scheduling account rather than by preference.

faq.q: If the wait is short, why does my US visa still take months?
faq.a: Because the appointment calendar is only the first of three stages, and in Nigeria it is not the binding one. After the interview a case can go into administrative processing, which is unpredictable and outside anyone's control. Passport return and delivery adds more. A published wait time measures the distance to the interview and nothing after it.

faq.q: Can I use the $750 paid expedite in Nigeria?
faq.a: No. The State Department's expedited appointment pilot runs only at designated missions, and as of 19 August 2026 those are Mission Mexico and Mission Canada. No Nigerian post participates. Given queues of about 15 to 30 days, there would be very little for it to buy in any case.

faq.q: Should I apply in Ghana or another neighbouring country instead?
faq.a: No, and it would be slower as well as riskier. Accra was around 105 days for visitor interviews in August 2026, several times Abuja's queue. More importantly, since the State Department's guidance of 6 September 2025, updated on 10 October 2025, applicants are directed to apply in their country of nationality or legal residence, and fees are neither refunded nor transferred if the plan fails.

faq.q: Do these figures apply to student visas?
faq.a: Student and exchange categories were around 15 days at both Nigerian posts in the same August 2026 snapshot, so the picture is similar. If your programme start date is close, the free expedited appointment request also exists for students within 60 days of a start date, with an original I-20 or DS-2019 and SEVIS fee evidence.

faq.q: Do I need a paid service to get an appointment in Nigeria?
faq.a: Almost certainly not, and we would rather say so than take the money. At a two to four week queue there is very little for a rescheduling service to improve. Book the first available appointment, prepare the application properly, and spend nothing. The value of a service like ours is in queues measured in hundreds of days, which is not what Nigeria has.

cta.heading: In Nigeria, the honest answer is that you probably do not need us
cta.body: A two to four week queue is not a problem a rescheduling service can meaningfully improve, and we will tell you that rather than take a fee for it. Where we are useful is a post with a queue measured in hundreds of days, which is what applicants in Canada, Australia and parts of India are facing. If you are applying in Nigeria and something specific has gone wrong, ask us anyway and we will point you at the right answer for free.
